one_line_contribution: A controlled dissociation, at matched rollout and token budgets, between transferring a reflective prompt optimizer's artifact (the optimized instruction skeleton) and transferring its accumulated diagnostic knowledge (a domain-scrubbed SYMPTOM/EDIT catalogue injected only into the reflection step), reported as a sample-efficiency Pareto curve with a crossover budget rather than a leaderboard win.
closest_prior_work: The Related Work engages GEPA, MIPROv2, PromptBreeder, REMO, SPoT/ATTEMPT and cross-model transfer, but omits the cluster that actually owns this idea: ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024) already harvests cross-task insights from success/failure trajectories into a retrievable natural-language rule pool with explicit ADD/EDIT/DOWNVOTE operators and already evaluates transfer to unseen tasks; Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025) accumulates reusable strategies as persistent test-time memory; ReasoningBank (2025) distills generalizable strategies from both successful and failed traces into a retrieved memory; and Agentic Context Engineering (2025) literally builds an evolving 'playbook' of bullet-level strategies from execution feedback and benchmarks it against GEPA. Against these, 'harvest failure->edit rules, retrieve by symptom match, inject into context' is not the new thing. What survives as new is narrower: the injection point is the optimizer's reflection step rather than the executor's context, and the paper's real object is the artifact-vs-search-knowledge dissociation plus the crossover-budget measurement. That is a legitimate delta but it is a controlled-ablation delta, not a new mechanism, and the proposal does not currently frame it that way or cite the works it must beat.
strongest_objection: The design's own scrubbing gate maximizes the probability of its own null. Rules must pass a leakage test in which a held-out LLM cannot identify the source task above chance (<=1/6), and each rule is capped at 60 tokens. A 60-token instruction that is provably uninformative about which of six tasks produced it is, almost by construction, generic prompt-engineering advice — which is exactly baseline (iv), the hand-written checklist. Domain-generality and retained diagnostic specificity are in direct tension here, and the proposal treats scrubbing as a pass/fail hygiene step rather than as the dial that determines whether there is a paper. The likely interleaving that kills the central claim: playbook beats cold-start by 3-8 points at 50 rollouts, and the hand-written checklist matches it within the noise floor — at which point, by the authors' own refutation criterion, the harvesting contributes nothing and the result is 'putting any competent advice in the reflection prompt helps small-budget GEPA', which is not an ICLR contribution. Two supporting problems compound it. (a) Source/target contamination on the most favorable pair: 2WikiMultiHop is a source and HotpotQA is a target — near-duplicate multi-hop QA with near-identical failure modes and output format — and BBH subsets appear on both sides, so 'six held-out target tasks' overstates the transfer distance for at least three of them. (b) Half of the hypothesis ('never induce negative transfer', 'never worse than cold-start by more than the noise floor on any target') is an accept-the-null claim, but the statistical plan only powers a 1.5-point aggregate paired difference at n=30; per-target non-inferiority at n=5 seeds is badly underpowered and no equivalence test (TOST or comparable) is specified. Separately, the promised crossover CI 'narrower than the checkpoint spacing' is not identifiable from checkpoints at 25/50/100/200/300 when the crossover is predicted at 120-250 — the interval would be an artifact of interpolation between two checkpoints 100 rollouts apart.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Run baseline (iv), the hand-written checklist, as a two-target pilot BEFORE the full harvest, and make scrub strength a measured dial rather than a gate: report a leakage-vs-benefit curve (source-identification accuracy on the x-axis, gain over cold-start on the y-axis). If the curve is flat, that is the paper's finding and it is publishable; if it slopes, the harvested content is doing work and the claim is established. 2) Add the in-domain self-harvested playbook baseline (see missing_baseline). 3) Remove the contaminated pairs — move 2WikiMultiHop out of the source pool or HotpotQA out of the targets, and require that no target task shares a suite with any source task — then report gains as a function of stated source-target distance rather than pooled. 4) Specify a non-inferiority test with a pre-registered margin for the no-negative-transfer half of the hypothesis, and state per-target power honestly (or make that claim only at the pooled level). 5) Log test score continuously or at 8-10 checkpoints so the crossover budget is actually identifiable, and drop the promise that its CI beats the checkpoint spacing. 6) Cut the arm matrix to fit the stated budget (see feasibility) and say explicitly which arms run on all six targets and which run on a two-target subset. 7) Reposition against ExpeL / Dynamic Cheatsheet / ReasoningBank / ACE, and make the dissociation-and-crossover measurement the stated contribution rather than the playbook mechanism.
missing_baseline: An in-domain self-harvested playbook: run GEPA on the target task for the first 25-50 rollouts, distill a failure->edit playbook from that task's own traces by the identical pipeline, and inject it for the remaining budget — no cross-domain source runs at all. This is the baseline that decides whether 'cross-domain transfer' is the contribution or whether any failure->edit memory mechanism (REMO-style, same-domain) captures the entire effect, and it costs almost nothing relative to the rest of the matrix. Neither the shuffled-playbook control (isolates content vs token count) nor the hand-written checklist (isolates harvesting vs generic advice) covers it. A second, cheaper omission: cold-start GEPA given the same wall-clock/token budget spent on more reflection calls or longer reflections, since 'playbook helps' and 'more reflection compute helps' are confounded when the playbook lengthens the reflection prompt.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty — no searches are reported, so novelty is asserted rather than established, and I weight that as a weakness rather than a neutral. The Related Work does cite 2025-2026 items (REMO, PromptBridge, Oved et al.), so the authors are not ignoring recency wholesale, but they searched the prompt-optimizer literature and not the agent-memory literature, which is where the collision actually lives. Specific works the check should have surfaced and rebutted: Agentic Context Engineering (2025), which builds an incrementally updated 'playbook' of strategies from execution feedback and explicitly benchmarks against GEPA — the single most dangerous collision, since it shares the name, the object, and the comparison; ReasoningBank (2025), which distills reusable strategies from successful and failed trajectories into a retrieved memory; Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025), persistent test-time memory of reusable tactics; and ExpeL (2023/AAAI 2024), which already does cross-task insight extraction with transfer evaluation. None of these, to my knowledge, runs the artifact-vs-search-knowledge dissociation at matched budgets with a crossover interval, so the proposal is not dead — but the burden is now on the authors to run that comparison against a memory-augmented baseline from this cluster, not against stateless GEPA alone, and a submission that reaches reviewers without naming these will be scored as unaware of its own neighbourhood.
